description: Issue #746 (Sprites half of the alias/Sprites shadowing fix, landed with #742): with `sprites` ACTIVE, redefining one of the profile's three turtle-identity reporters raises `ol-reserved-word` with `namespace` `primitive`. `spec/tooling.md:185` is a normative Layer-2 "Required behavior" row — declaring a built-in name (a keyword, a **primitive**, or an alias spelling of one) at a declaration slot raises `ol-reserved-word` — and `:175-176` requires it be applied against the active profile set. `new_turtle`/`who`/`turtles` are Sprites **primitives** (`spec/turtles-and-sprites.md`'s "Canonical forms" table: each Kind-R, arity 0), so with the profile claimed they must collide exactly as `grid` (Geometry), `set_tempo` (Sound), `dict` (Data), and `wait` (Interaction & Events) already did; before this fix the Sprites table was simply never consulted and `define who` was silently accepted, leaving a claimed profile with a normative requirement unmet. Note the `namespace` is `primitive`, NOT `reserved`: the reporters are ordinary primitives, unlike the block-heads `tell`/`ask`/`each`, which `spec/turtles-and-sprites.md:154` reserves and which the sibling `reserved-procedures-with-sprites` fixture pins as `reserved`. The two categories are reported by different branches and must not be conflated. Paired with `reserved-reporters-without-sprites`, which checks this exact source under Core+Turtle alone and is clean. `"check": true` (semantic-checker only, no execution) because this is a checker rule: the procedures are never called and no events are produced.

diagnostics.message: new_turtle is already a primitive, so it can't be redefined here.
who is already a primitive, so it can't be redefined here.
turtles is already a primitive, so it can't be redefined here.
